messages:
Carol: customer reported possible unauthorized access to their Dedicated env — they saw unexpected reads from their model checkpoints bucket. pinging security.
Kevin: thanks. is this Dedicated or Private (VPC)? any customer-provided KMS keys? :eyes:
Carol: Dedicated (redwood-dedicated-us-east-2). They said KMS CMK is customer-managed. Customer ID: acct-9382. Reported IPs: 52.84.###.### (they redacted).
ops-bot: ALERT: suspicious_kms_decrypt detected for key arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01 (severity: high) — rule matched: anomalous-source-ip
Marta: pulling audit logs now. running CloudTrail filter for KMS Decrypt + S3:GetObject for acct-9382. will post sample lines.
Marta: ```
Timestamp: 2024-11-21T18:12:03Z
eventName: Decrypt
userIdentity: AWSService: redwood-runtime
sourceIPAddress: 52.84.123.45
requestParameters: {"keyId":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01"}
responseElements: null
```
Marta: and corresponding S3 access:
Marta: ```
Timestamp: 2024-11-21T18:12:04Z
eventName: GetObject
bucket: customer-acct-9382-models
key: checkpoint-2024-11-20.tar.gz
sourceIPAddress: 52.84.123.45
userAgent: aws-sdk-nodejs/3.x
```
Sanjay: that IP doesn't match any of our known edge ranges for that account. looks like a service principal key was used from an unexpected host.
Kevin: immediate containment: 1) revoke runtime credentials for acct-9382 2) rotate CMK access policy to deny new decrypts until we verify 3) block source IP at firewall/route table for dedicated pool. Marta, can you revoke creds now and stage policy change?
Marta: revoking creds: `aws sts revoke-session --session-id session-9a7b` (done). updated CMK policy to add temporary deny for `Decrypt` for the runtime principal. applied network block for 52.84.123.45 via ACL.
Carol: customer notified: "we saw unusual access, we've isolated resources and are investigating. will share logs and next steps." they asked for timeline.
Alice: opening incident ticket (INC-2024-5923) and adding legal/compliance. tagging customer-security channel to track comms.
Kevin: list of things we need to collect: a) full CloudTrail + KMS logs (90d) b) runtime audit trail of token issuance c) host/container logs for that time window d) mapping of which models/checkpoints accessed. Sanjay can you export and drop in secure workspace?
Sanjay: exporting logs now. ETA ~25m. I'll upload to /secure/incidents/INC-2024-5923/logs with access restricted to security+legal+SE.
Kevin: good. also check if the service principal key was used elsewhere. search for same session ID across accounts.
Marta: found 3 Decrypt events with same session id across two objects. Looks scoped to acct-9382 only.
ops-bot: NOTE: automatic detection rule triggered escalation flow — added label "customer-impact" and set severity to P2.
Carol: customer wants proof no exfil beyond those objects. we'll provide redacted logs and timeline after internal review. dont share key material.
Kevin: post-incident actions (initial): 1) add RBAC change: disallow cross-account runtime key access by default 2) enforce MFA for key rotation ops 3) create alert for KMS decrypts from non-customer IP ranges 4) improve runbook steps for dedicated env containment
Alice: will assign owners and schedule a blameless postmortem. propose 1 week post containment.
Carol: thanks all. I'll keep customer updated every 2 hours until we have full scope. :white_check_mark:
